correctness.rationale: For a three-prime-support integer n=p^a q^b r^c the positive integer G(n) is forced to 1 and p=2 from strict geometric-tail bounds. Clearing denominators and reducing mod the highest prime power gives m(1+s+...+s^{e-1})≡1 (mod s^e). At Ω=3 this forces q=3,r=5. At Ω=4 the exhaustive exponent patterns 2²qr,2q²r,2qr² lead respectively to q=5,r=19; q=3,r=17; and a parity contradiction. The q² branch uses d=(2q²-1)/r odd <2q plus d≡-2(q+1) mod q², ruling q>=5; r² case uses quotient parity mod4. Each of 30,306,380 satisfies G=1 by independent exact reciprocal arithmetic. Proof has no size cutoff; a scan up to 200000 cannot establish exhaustive scope.
